html:
The prince of the Mandinka people who founded the Mali Empire in the 13th century. His life is told in the Epic of Sundiata, still sung by griots across West Africa.

Much of what we know comes from that oral epic. In the epic, Sundiata is the son of a Mande king and Sogolon, an ugly but powerful woman. As a child he cannot walk and is mocked, until one day he stands and pulls up a baobab tree. Jealous rivals drive him and his mother into exile.

Meanwhile Sumanguru Kanté, the sorcerer king of Sosso, conquers the Mande lands. The Mande clans call Sundiata home. He gathers an army and defeats Sumanguru at the Battle of Kirina, around 1235.

As ruler, or mansa, Sundiata united the Mande clans. Tradition says a great assembly at Kurukan Fuga set out the laws and duties of each clan. His empire grew rich from the gold and trade of the old empire of Ghana. A later relative, Mansa Musa, made Mali famous across the world.
